name: OZD ImageFileX – Image Converter & Text Graphics
author: Sadık Özdoğan

sections.description:
OZD ImageFileX is a privacy-friendly image converter and text graphics plugin that works entirely inside the WordPress administration area. Convert Media Library files or images uploaded from your computer to JPEG, PNG, WebP, or AVIF; resize or crop them; and save the results to WordPress or download them individually or as a ZIP file.

No account, API key, or external image-processing service is required. Original Media Library files are not overwritten.

Why use OZD ImageFileX?

  • Process images privately on your own WordPress server.
  • Convert selected images or the entire Media Library with no total image limit and no external account.
  • Regenerate registered WordPress, theme, and plugin image sizes for existing attachments.
  • Keep original Media Library files unchanged.
  • Prepare images using ready-made dimensions for popular social media platforms.
  • Turn text into shareable graphics without leaving WordPress.
  • Save converted files to the Media Library, download them, or do both.

Image conversion

  • Select one or more images from the WordPress Media Library.
  • Upload up to 30 images in one request, with a maximum of 20 MB per file.
  • Create JPEG, PNG, WebP, and AVIF output when the server supports the selected format.
  • Resize while preserving the aspect ratio or crop to exact dimensions.
  • Set width, height, and output quality.
  • Save results to the Media Library, download them, or do both.
  • Download multiple results as a ZIP file when ZipArchive is available.
  • Apply common Instagram, Facebook, and LinkedIn dimensions.

Separate tool tabs

  • Single Image Conversion accepts one Media Library image or one uploaded file.
  • Bulk Image Conversion accepts multiple files or the entire Media Library.
  • Regenerate Image Sizes, Social Media, Text to Image, System Status, Help, Documentation, Support, and Settings remain separate tool tabs.
  • Tools use an accessible tablist with tab/tabpanel roles, aria-selected, and linked panel labels. Left/Right arrows move tab focus; Home/End reach the first/last tab; Enter or Space activates it. Tab moves into the active panel.
  • Switching tabs loads content without a page reload and retains visited tool nodes, form values, and ongoing jobs. Browser Back/Forward restores the tab URL. Loading failures preserve the current tool.
  • All tools share a connected folder-style tab strip. The selected tab joins the white content panel. On narrow screens the strip scrolls horizontally, keeping labels readable. Keyboard focus remains visible and the active tab is brought into view. Without JavaScript, links retain server-rendered navigation.
  • Success and error notices distinguish one image, batches, and image-size regeneration.

Whole-library conversion

  • Administrators can select Entire Media Library, preview all image attachments with 20 per page, and process the entire snapshot.
  • Media Library selections larger than 30 are supported. There is no total library selection or job limit.
  • Images are processed one at a time in bounded requests; new output copies are not added to the running job.
  • Per-image results include source ID, filename, success/error, size statistics where applicable, and download/media links.
  • Separate success and failure counters remain visible during processing. Completion explicitly identifies batches with failed images. Filter failed images and browse all result pages; normal per-image errors do not stop later images.
  • Download the finished ZIP, then use Return to ImageFileX to clear results and return to the form. Results stay visible until you choose to return; no automatic redirect interrupts downloads.
  • Pause after the current image and resume remaining images on the same page. Keep the page open; leaving/reloading discards its in-memory queue. A stalled request has a 90-second client deadline; uncertain outcomes pause the job and are never retried automatically.
  • Global authorization loss pauses the job. Each attachment still requires edit permission.
  • Conversion creates new files and media records when saving; it does not replace existing page URLs or original attachments.
  • The existing request/ZIP workflow for direct uploads and selections of up to 30 remains available. In sequential mode, successful outputs are collected into a combined ZIP in chunks of up to 20 files when ZipArchive is available. A ZIP failure pauses sequential conversion; retry the ZIP and resume, or explicitly continue with individual downloads. Individual links are shown when the job finishes (or after choosing to continue without ZIP), preventing early downloads from disrupting ZIP assembly. The ZIP link expires 30 minutes after finalization; individual links expire 30 minutes after creation. Very large archives still depend on server disk space and ZIP processing resources.

Regenerate registered image sizes

  • Open Regenerate Image Sizes to view dimensions and crop rules registered by WordPress, the active theme, and plugins.
  • Process selected Media Library images or, for administrators, the entire library.
  • Choose which registered sizes to rebuild.
  • Create missing/incorrectly sized thumbnails, including physically missing files that still have metadata, or regenerate all selected sizes.
  • New sub-size files are linked to the existing attachment ID and metadata; the main image and old thumbnail files are retained. Old thumbnail cleanup and replacement of URLs already embedded in page content are not included.
  • Missing mode compares dimensions and file existence; changed crop rules at the same dimensions require all-sizes mode.
  • Use the current attached main image as the source, preserving prior WordPress crops/rotations and filename edit hashes used by responsive srcset. The larger pre-edit/original upload is not substituted.
  • Respect WordPress crop/scale rules without enlarging smaller sources. Sizes requiring no downsize are skipped.
  • Regeneration uses normal WordPress image-editor encoding and output-format filters; conversion compression settings are not applied automatically.
  • Show per-image created/skipped counts and errors, including partial regeneration when one size fails.
  • Source files must be readable local files in the uploads directory. Remote-only/offloaded media must be restored locally first. Processing limits remain 20 MB, 8192 pixels per side, 40 million source pixels, and 12 million target pixels. GIF/SVG regeneration is not supported.
  • CSS-only dimensions cannot be discovered automatically; the theme must register actual image sizes.

Image optimization and compression

  • Keep the source format (JPEG, PNG, WebP, or AVIF) or choose another output format.
  • Select Standard conversion to retain the 1.0.0 encoding behavior.
  • Choose lossy JPEG, WebP, or AVIF compression and control quality from 1 to 100.
  • Choose lossless PNG compression or true lossless WebP encoding.
  • PNG always uses lossless compression; lossy PNG is not offered.
  • Detect Imagick builds that ignore lossy WebP quality using a small in-memory codec probe. Use a compatible GD encoder instead when available; otherwise return an explanation. No source images or external services are used for this check.
  • Lossless WebP requires an Imagick build with WebP support, or GD with PHP 8.1+ and IMG_WEBP_LOSSLESS. The produced WebP bitstream is checked before keeping the result.
  • JPEG and AVIF lossless encoding are not supported. Unsupported combinations return an explanation instead of silently producing a lossy image.
  • Compare original and output file sizes and the percentage reduction or increase for each successful result.
  • Fit images within width and height limits, preserve the aspect ratio, or crop using the existing controls. Smaller images are not enlarged.

Lossless refers to compression of the processed image pixels. Resizing, cropping, EXIF orientation, color-space conversion, and the server image editor’s bit-depth/alpha handling may alter source pixels. Original metadata and file bytes are not preserved by re-encoding. Quality is ignored in lossless mode. Compression cannot guarantee a smaller file; increases are reported. Size statistics compare the input and main output file, excluding generated Media Library thumbnails. Original files remain unchanged.

Text graphics

  • Turn text into shareable graphics with bundled DejaVu Sans, Noto Sans, and Open Sans fonts.
  • Control font weight, font size, colors, padding, line height, quality, and alignment.
  • Use GD with FreeType or Imagick, depending on the server configuration.

Privacy and security

  • Review image-library and format support on the System Status screen.
  • Use random, user-bound download links that expire after 30 minutes.
  • Keep download-only output in the server temporary directory.
  • Remove downloaded files immediately and clean abandoned temporary files with a scheduled task.
  • Allow only logged-in users with the upload_files capability to process images.

Languages

The source language is English and a complete Turkish translation is bundled. Administrators can choose Use the WordPress language, Turkish, or English from OZD ImageFileX > Settings. Additional WordPress.org language packs can be added later without changing the plugin architecture.

Explicit converter output formats are protected from thumbnail output-format remapping during the save operation only. Editors without support for the requested target format are excluded, including in standard mode. Failed output verification distinguishes empty files, unreadable images, and MIME mismatches.

The plugin uses the WordPress image editor API for normal image conversion. WordPress selects an available compatible editor, such as GD or Imagick.

External services and privacy

All image and text processing takes place on the WordPress server. OZD ImageFileX does not send uploaded images, entered text, site information, or usage data to ImageFileX or another external service.

The Help, Documentation, and Support screens contain optional links to pages operated by the plugin author on imagefilex.com:

  • Help: https://www.imagefilex.com/sayfa.php?sayfa=yardim
  • Frequently asked questions: https://www.imagefilex.com/sayfa.php?sayfa=sss
  • Contact: https://www.imagefilex.com/sayfa.php?sayfa=iletisim
  • Privacy policy: https://www.imagefilex.com/sayfa.php?sayfa=gizlilik-politikasi
  • Terms of use: https://www.imagefilex.com/sayfa.php?sayfa=kullanim-sozlesmesi

No connection to imagefilex.com is made unless an administrator opens one of these links. Opening an external page sends the normal web request information, such as the visitor’s IP address and browser headers, directly to imagefilex.com. It does not send images or text processed by the plugin.

Third-party licenses

Bundled font attribution, source, and license information is available in THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.txt.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin ZIP from Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin, or install it from the WordPress.org Plugin Directory.
  2. Activate OZD ImageFileX.
  3. Open OZD ImageFileX from the WordPress administration menu.
  4. Review the System Status tab before using WebP, AVIF, ZIP, or text-to-image features.
  5. Optionally choose the plugin language from OZD ImageFileX > Settings.
sections.faq:
Does the plugin add a shortcode or public upload form?

No. All tools run in the WordPress administration area. Image-processing actions require a logged-in user with the upload_files capability.

Is GD required?

No. Standard image conversion uses the WordPress image editor API, which can use GD or Imagick. Text-to-image generation requires either GD with FreeType or Imagick.

Why is AVIF or WebP unavailable?

Format support depends on the GD or Imagick build installed by the hosting provider. Review the System Status screen for the capabilities detected on the server.

Are original Media Library files overwritten?

No. The plugin creates a new, uniquely named output file.

What happens to download-only files?

Download links are random, tied to the current user, and expire after 30 minutes. Download-only files are stored in the server temporary directory and deleted after download. A daily scheduled task removes abandoned plugin temporary files.

How do I change the plugin language?

Open OZD ImageFileX > Settings and choose Use the WordPress language, Turkish, or English. The setting affects OZD ImageFileX only.

Does the plugin send my images to imagefilex.com?

No. Image and text processing is local to the WordPress server. The plugin connects to imagefilex.com only when an administrator chooses to open an external help, FAQ, or contact link.
sections.changelog:
1.1.0

  • Use a connected folder-style tab strip for every tool, documentation, support, and settings; keep accessible roles and keyboard activation.

  • Add accessible tablist/tab/tabpanel semantics, manual keyboard activation, linked labels and selected states.

  • Load tab panels without page reload; retain tool settings and listeners when returning to visited tabs.

  • Separate single-image and bulk conversion tabs; improve responsive tab navigation and active/focus states.

  • Distinguish single-image, batch, and image-size regeneration completion/error notices.

  • Fix explicit output format remapping and standard-mode target encoder selection.

  • Add combined ZIP downloads for sequential library jobs, clearer success/failure counters, detailed encoding errors, and a manual return-to-form button.

  • Added a registered-image-size regeneration tab with selected/all-library processing, missing/all modes, original retention, and per-size metadata verification.

  • Added unlimited-total Media Library conversion through sequential requests, paged previews/results, per-image errors, progress, and same-page pause/resume.
  • Added snapshot boundaries excluding output copies from running jobs, per-image permissions, regeneration locks, and bounded request deadlines.
  • Preserved direct-upload and small-selection conversion/ZIP workflows.
  • Added explicit standard, lossy, and lossless compression modes to the existing image conversion workflow.
  • Added optimized lossless PNG and true lossless WebP output with codec verification.
  • Added a keep-source-format option for JPEG, PNG, WebP, and AVIF.
  • Added per-image source size, output size, and percentage reduction or increase.
  • Kept original files, existing conversion defaults, crop controls, social presets, text graphics, and secure download workflows.
  • Avoided no-op resize failures when a source already fits the requested dimensions.
  • Added validation of encoded outputs and cleanup of failed output files.
  • Updated interface guidance and Turkish translations.

1.0.0

  • Initial release.
  • Added Media Library and direct-upload conversion workflows.
  • Added aspect-ratio-preserving resize, crop, quality, and pixel controls.
  • Added bulk conversion, secure downloads, and ZIP downloads.
  • Added Instagram, Facebook, and LinkedIn presets.
  • Added text-to-image generation with bundled fonts and GD/Imagick support.
  • Added System Status, Help, Documentation, Support, and Settings screens.
  • Added English source strings, a complete Turkish translation, and a plugin language selector.
  • Added the Ozdemag\ImageFileX namespace and ozdemag-prefixed global identifiers.
